Adverse effects may be limited by starting with a low dose: one suggested regimen1 starts with trihexyphenidyl 1 mg daily and rises up to 12 mg daily over the next 4 to 6 weeks; some patients may require up to 60 to 100 mg daily. The BNFC sug- gests that children aged 1 month to 18 years may be given oral doses of 1 to 2 mg daily in 1 or 2 divided doses, adjusted accord- ing to response. 1. Jankovic J. Dystonia: medical therapy and botulinum toxin. Adv Neurol 2004; 94: 275–86.
